agent.title: Scanning agents
agent.whyShort: A scan does not happen without an agent connected inside the network being measured.
agent.tokenWarning: The platform stores its hash, not the secret. If you close this window without copying it, the token is lost and you have to revoke the agent and register another one.
agent.tokenNextStep: Copy it and deploy the agent inside the network you want to measure: the steps are right below.
agent.noneConnected: No agent is connected. Until one is, scans stay queued and nothing comes out.
agent.emptyBody: An agent is a process running inside the customer network. Without it, this platform cannot see what is in that network: from outside, it is unreachable.

form.intro: The agent is enrolled here and then deployed inside the customer network. It only needs HTTPS egress to the platform; it needs no inbound ports open.

form.system: Where is it going to be deployed?
form.systemWhy: The agent is a dependency-free Python script, so it runs the same on Linux, Windows Server and macOS. What changes are the paths and how it is left running, and this answer picks the instructions you get.

agent.setupCalloutTitle: There is an agent that has never connected
agent.setupCalloutBody: That is almost always a deployment with the token pasted wrong, not a platform failure. Here are the three steps, with your URL and your system already filled in.

limits.vulnerabilitiesTitle: What this scan does not say
limits.vulnerabilities: The agent measures what is there, not whether it is vulnerable. Crossing the inventory against the CVE database is the platform's job: here you only see the measurement. The vulnerabilities of these targets come from scanning their services.
limits.rpm: An image with RPM packages does not give up its inventory: the format is binary and the agent does not interpret it. The package count for that image is a zero that does not mean it has no packages.
limits.sinBaseDePaquetes: The package database (neither apk nor dpkg) does not appear in the image. Without it there is no way to know what is inside, so it is declared instead of returning an empty inventory.
limits.prefijoTruncado: The prefix contained {{total}} addresses and this agent analyses at most {{maximo}}. The scan was truncated to those {{maximo}} addresses: split the network into parts to measure all of it.
limits.privateRegistryBody: The agent carries no credentials, on purpose. A private registry returns an authentication error and the image cannot be read.
limits.dockerSocketBody: What is read is the image, not what is running. Live containers, their environment variables and their mounts are not visible from here.

differs.linux: On Linux: the file goes in /etc/fenix-agent/ and it is left running with systemd. Copy the block below and you are done.
differs.windows: On Windows Server: the file goes in C:\ProgramData\FenixAgent\ and it is left running with Task Scheduler, which ships with the system. Copy the block below and you are done.
differs.macos: On macOS: the file goes in /usr/local/etc/fenix-agent/ and it is left running with launchd. Copy the block below and you are done.
differs.desconocido: We do not know which system you are installing on. Pick yours above: the three steps are the same and only the file path and the startup block change. If you are not sure, look at where the file is kept on the machine: if it is under /etc/..., it is Linux.

setup.intro: The agent runs inside the network you want to measure. It only needs Python and outbound HTTPS to the platform: it asks for no inbound ports, which is what makes it installable in a production network without a firewall exception.
setup.needsBody: Python 3.11 or later, nothing else: the module uses only the standard library, so installing it on a segmented network does not mean pulling packages from outside.
setup.noToken: The token cannot be shown here: the platform stores its hash, not the secret, and it cannot be requested again. Copy the block, leave the placeholder in place, and substitute the real token when you have it in front of you.
setup.permissionsBody: The agent creates its results directory with 0700 permissions, which on Linux leaves the file readable only by its owner. Windows has no POSIX permissions: the 0700 is ignored and what protects the file is the folder's ACL. Restrict it to the service user and to administrators, or the scan results stay readable by anyone on the machine.
setup.permissionsTitle: File permissions are not the same on Windows
setup.serviceDescription: Mind Guard Fenix Team scanning agent
setup.stepIniBody: On the machine where the agent will run. The [plataforma] section and the url and token keys are not translated: the agent reads them, not a person.
setup.stepRunBody: In the foreground, so you can see the output. If it prints "agente registrado" with its identifier, the connection works.
setup.stepService: Leave it running as a service

stepServiceBody.linux: Save the unit in /etc/systemd/system/, reload systemd and enable it. An agent that goes down and does not come back stops launching scans, and a scan that never starts looks exactly like a scan that does not exist.
stepServiceBody.windows: Run this in an elevated PowerShell prompt. It registers the task with Task Scheduler, which ships with Windows Server, so it starts with the system. It is not sc.exe because a Python process is not a Windows service: it would start and die immediately, and the SCM would restart it in a loop.
stepServiceBody.macos: Save the plist in /Library/LaunchDaemons/ and load it with launchctl. KeepAlive makes it come back on its own if it goes down.
stepServiceBody.desconocido: Save the unit in /etc/systemd/system/, reload systemd and enable it. If your machine does not use systemd, the previous step —running it in the foreground—is enough and the agent stays in the foreground.

setup.title: How to deploy the agent
setup.urlMissing: This panel is being served without an API URL, so the block comes out with no url and the agent will not start.
setup.urlMissingWhy: It is the VITE_API_URL variable on the frontend. In development it is left empty on purpose because the browser goes through the Vite proxy, but to pull the configuration file out you need the real one: https://api.mindguardredteam.com in production, or http://localhost:8000 if the agent runs on the same machine.
setup.verifyBody: Come back to this screen and reload. The badge goes from "Never connected" to "Connected" as soon as the agent registers its first heartbeat, which is every fifteen seconds by default. If it does not change, the agent log has the reason: almost always a mistyped token or a URL that is not the public one.
